The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons has recorded 1,508 cases of human trafficking and related offences, leading to the arrest of 1,434 suspects between August 2025 and the period under review. The Director-General of NAPTIP, Binta Bello, disclosed this at the 29th National Stakeholders Consultative Forum on Human Trafficking in Nigeria and the 3rd Policy-Level Meeting held in Abuja. Bello, in a statement posted on NAPTIP’s Facebook page on Tuesday, said the agency also received and rehabilitated 2,700 victims within the period, while 65 cases involving 85 persons were initiated in court. She added that 74 cases resulted in the conviction of 97 persons for human trafficking offences. The DG further disclosed that since its establishment, NAPTIP had rescued and supported 28,762 victims and secured 857 convictions against human trafficking offenders. She highlighted the Agency’s intensified efforts against technology-facilitated trafficking, deceptive online recruitment and other emerging forms of exploitation, alongside strengthened intelligence gathering, victim protection and international cooperation. Bello also called for the urgent establishment of a NAPTIP State Command in Delta State, describing it as the only state without the agency’s presence. She said the command would strengthen the agency’s operational response and improve victim protection in the state. Meanwhile, the Federal Government has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening Nigeria’s response to human trafficking through improved institutional support, policy backing and adequate funding for NAPTIP and other stakeholders. The Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, gave the assurance while declaring the forum open. Represented by the Acting Director, Citizens Rights Department, Federal Ministry of Justice, Kabiru Haliru, the minister commended NAPTIP and its partners for their achievements in prosecution, victim rescue and rehabilitation, public awareness and policy development. He stressed the need for sustained political commitment, stronger partnerships and adequate resources to tackle human trafficking. The forum, which brought together stakeholders, including the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, International Organisation for Migration, International Centre for Migration Policy Development, FIAP and NACTAL, was convened to review progress and strengthen collaboration.
